articleTitle: Recommending Graduate Admission Using Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Potential scholars are often faced with the challenge of picking which institutions to submit applications to for degree courses. Although a lot of forecasters and advisors are available to help students, decisions are based on only a few instances of prior enrolment. Thus, they can occasionally be accurate. The majority of prognosis algorithms in use today were created using machine learning (ML) techniques. We provide a stacking ensemble framework to forecast and assess educational achievement in courses of study. To increase precision, three techniques for ML are constructed in the preliminary stage: Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), and Naïve Bayes (NB). Logistic regression (LR) is subsequently added through stacking. For every applicant, the algorithm generates a recommendation for entrance to the institution of their choice based on an algorithmic approach that takes into account their interests and educational experiences. We built the computational framework to leverage information from a real-time admissions dataset of 500 grads. Recall, accuracy, precision, and F1-score are the 4 assessment indicators used in the present study. Comparative investigations show that the suggested model outperforms the individual base models. The evaluation’s key factors may be interpreted and leveraged as a guide for choosing possible candidates for enrolment.

articleTitle: Hybrid Algorithm to Upgrade Voltage Stability Index and Real Power Loss Reduction Using Reconfiguration in Radial Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The intelligent algorithm for developing radial distribution systems (RDS) is the critical objective for power engineers. The proposed hybrid algorithm blends the particle swarm optimization (PSO) and genetic algorithm (GA) to get an optimal energy-efficient solution. This paper's objective function combines actual real power loss (PL) and voltage stability index (VSI). The achievement of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated using IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus RDS.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Cotton Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Cotton plant diseases significantly impact developing nations' economies and pose a threat to the textile industry. Detecting these diseases is challenging due to lack of competence and fluctuating disease stages. Recent technology has enabled the use of computer-aided techniques to automatically identify and categorize disorders. This paper proposes various deep learning approaches for identifying and categorizing cotton leaf diseases, focusing on unhealthy and unhealthy areas. The study uses a dataset and various optimization techniques, with the Xception model showing the highest validation accuracy of 98.61% using the Adam optimizer.

articleTitle: Kidnapped Vehicle Using Particle Filters-Self-Driving Car Nanodegree
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Detecting and tracking stolen vehicles is an important task with self-driving cars. This study focuses on the use of particle filters to detect and track stolen vehicles. Particle filters are a probabilistic estimation method that can effectively handle the uncertainties and nonlinearities associated with vehicle tracking. The study examines the application of particle filters in the Nanodegree project to self-driving cars, specifically for the detection and tracking of stolen vehicles. The results demonstrate the efficiency of particle filters to accurately estimate the location and routes of hijacked vehicles, enabling effective recovery operations Vehicle occupied scenarios refer to situations in which a self-driving vehicle loses its location awareness The vehicle can measure its position observations based on a sensor. Using small- scale filters, this research aims to improve the ability of self- driving vehicles to reconstruct reality, accurately restoring its position in cases where they are unpredictable, ultimately contributing to the robustness and reliability of autonomous vehicle systems.

articleTitle: Improving Public Security: Application of YOLOv7 for Vehicle Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This research paper focuses on the practical implementation of the YOLOv7 deep learning model for vehicle detection in real-time which is quite necessary for modern intelligent transportation systems (ITS). In the course of increased demand for smart vehicle detections to handle traffic efficiently and ensure safety, this study evaluates the YOLOv7 model performance in different traffic and environmental scenarios. A large dataset with a diversity of scenes including urban and rural scenes across different light conditions is used to train and test the model; for this purpose, emphasis is placed on precision and efficiency. The work discusses an advanced methodology involving refined training methods, exact testing standards, and evaluation of the output using metrics that include precision, recall, F1-score, and Intersection over Union (IoU). The outcomes reveal the YOLOv7’s potential in detecting class objects with high precision and recall in all scenarios, and it is apparent that the model is the most accurate in a daytime environment of rural areas. Results will be interpreted and it will be revealed that YOLOv7 is a promising object detection model for ITS that can improve real-time data processing profoundly, though weak performance in low-light conditions calls for there is still room for further enhancement. Therefore, the conclusion proves the model to be scalable and also the possibility of its integration into ITS applications. Nevertheless, more efforts are needed to establish effective autonomous and semi-autonomous vehicle technologies. This study enhances the field of vehicle detection technology by contributing findings that orient researchers toward higher-level and reliable ITS implementations. The ultimate recommendations are aimed toward YOLOv7 as the default model in the evolving development of traffic monitoring systems globally.

articleTitle: Predicting Mobile Prices with Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Smartphones are increasingly vital to people on a daily basis. Telephones are utilized in all aspects of life, ranging from personal to professional, due to technological advancements. It serves a function beyond making phone calls. It enables internet connectivity and email reading. when not using the computer. The characteristics of a mobile phone are a crucial consideration when buying one.The overall objective of this research is to find the best way to apply machine learning to estimate the retail pricing of smartphones based on their individual specs. Individuals who frequently use their phone are more attentive to selecting features. When purchasing a cell phone, a comparison is done based on the price-performance ratio. Phone features are regarded as performance. This research aims to forecast if mobile phones with certain features are considered economical or expensive.This work is capable of being utilized in various marketing and business contexts to assist in making informed purchasing decisions by maximizing features while minimizing costs.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Cyber Security Incident Response with Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Smart contracts have emerged as a promising and innovative technology to enhance cyber-security incident response. With the rise of cyber-security incidents, traditional incident response systems often face challenges in terms of efficiency, transparency and reliability. Smart contracts based on blockchain technology provide a way using circuits and an automated approach to streamline incident response activities. This paper examines the potential of smart contracts in cyber- security incident response, discussing their benefits and challenges. Highlight key features of smart contracts that enable safe and effective incident response, such as automated incident reporting, evidence protection, integrated response actions and, in this case, potential limitations and security considerations of smart contracts were addressing. Overall, smart contracts have the potential to transform cyber-security incident response by providing a secure and transparent framework for industry collaboration and automation

articleTitle: A Proposed Method to Extend One-Bit of the Parallel Interface in a Digital to Analog Conversion Circuit by Adding an External Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to extend one bit to a parallel interface type Digital to Analog conversion circuit by using an external device. The examination of the Digital to Analog conversion circuit's principle is conducted in order to perform the aforementioned extension. Additionally, an analysis is carried out to identify the problems that arise when extending one bit using additional individual devices. Subsequently, a bit extension system for the Digital to Analog conversion device is proposed, utilizing an operational amplifier circuit. This method is utilising the high-precision characteristics of the operational amplifier, which affects the size of the output waveform only even when an error occurs in the device, and the voltage reversal phenomenon occurring between the bits doesn’t take place. To verify the effectiveness of the method proposed, we constructed the circuitry for experiment and measured the absolute voltage and relative error of the output waveform. According to the experimental results, it was confirmed that only 0.0756% error occurred on average compared to the 12-bit class Digital to Analog converter. According to these results, we confirmed that one bit extension is possible by adding a small number of individual devices.

articleTitle: Inferencing Age and Gender from Facial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The increasing use of social media and platforms has made automatic age and gender classification a crucial task for a variety of applications. Still, current approaches frequently perform less than optimally when faced with real-world image data, especially when compared to the significant advancements shown in face recognition tasks. Here, we demonstrate how deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can learn effective representations and hence considerably improve performance on certain tasks. We present a simplified convolutional network design that remains effective in situations where training material is scarce. We use strict preprocessing methods to extract gender and age relevant characteristics from CNNs, and then we use specialized classifiers to classify the images. Our empirical findings demonstrate the greater accuracy and resilience of our suggested methodology over the most recent techniques, especially when applied to real-world datasets. We believe that this will contribute to the advancement of automatic age and gender classification systems, with potential applications in various domains such as social media analytics, marketing research, and personalized content recommendation.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Multi-modal Content-Based approach to Graph-based Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This study offers a novel architecture based on graphs and is intended to improve the representation of user-item interactions in recommendation systems. Due to the utilisation of bipartite graph; decomposition and heterogeneous message propagation; this technique successfully captures intricate user-item interactions. Systems uses graph convolutional networks (GCN) and meta-path-based graph neural networks (GNN) to store features that make the user-item interaction space more dependable. A GCN decoder reconstructs the user-item interaction network to enhance system understanding, while a multi-class classifier enables personalised recommendations based on the user’s preferences. A combined loss propagation mechanism, advanced similarity matching, and link prediction methods improve the recommendation process. This makes the digital platform more accurate and customer-satisfying. The proposed method, after validation on real-world video datasets surpassed the recent techniques.

articleTitle: AI Guardian on the Road: Harnessing Machine Learning for Two-Wheeler Helmet Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study and implementation of a vehicle helmet detection system aimed at enhancing road safety measures using advanced computer techniques that involve real-time surveillance. Wearing helmets significantly reduces the risk of severe head injuries in road accidents by providing a crucial protective barrier against impact forces during the collision. This safety measure acts as a pivotal safeguard, mitigating the direct effects of collisions and reducing the probability of traumatic brain injuries or fatal head trauma. This protection is essential for threatening the direct impact of accidents and underrating the chances of severe head harms or certain damage. According to the 2023 report each World Health Organization (WHO), promoting helmets right can lower the risk of deadly harms by 42% and the risk of head harms by 69%. The system is capable of analysing traffic video footage to identify moving objects and classify vehicles further the system incorporates a helmet detection component to ensure compliance with safety regulations by verifying whether both the rider and pillion passengers are wearing helmets.

articleTitle: Evolving Landscapes: A Comprehensive Analysis of Educational Technology Websites and Strategies for Enhanced Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The field of educational technology (edtech) is often described as rapidly evolving, a sentiment frequently used to encourage senior managers to adopt new technologies promptly. However, despite this urgency, the edtech sector lacks a robust record of its own history or critical reflection on its development. Audrey Watters recently sought recommendations for books on the history of educational technology, revealing a scarcity of such resources. While previous studies have analyzed edtech websites and marketing strategies, this comprehensive investigation offers a unique multi-faceted approach. By combining website analytics, student surveys, and competitor benchmarking, our study provides actionable insights tailored to the evolving needs of edtech programs like Boise State University's EDTECH department. The findings have far-reaching implications for enhancing online presence, user experience, and enrollment across educational institutions.

articleTitle: Exploiting the domain of Deep Learning for Brain Tumor Classification: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Brain tumors (BT) constitute a formidable challenge globally, affecting both adults and children and exhibiting poor survival rates. Their diverse types, characterized by location, texture, and morphology, underscore the importance of accurate classification to guide appropriate treatment decisions early on. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) emerges as a pivotal modality for BT differentiation. However, manual analysis of MRI data is time-intensive and prone to human errors, necessitating the development of automated Computer-Assisted Diagnosis (CAD) systems. Recent strides in image classification, particularly deep learning (DL) hold promise in this realm. To this end, we employed Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)s to devise a novel model comprising multiple layers for MRI brain tumor classification. Through experimental validation across three datasets, our approach demonstrated compelling performance compared to existing methodologies.

articleTitle: Emotionally Intelligent Edtech: A CNN Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This study addresses the absence of immediate emotional feedback in online education by utilizing computer vision and deep learning to create a real-time emotion recognition system. Despite encountering technological and privacy challenges, the system enriches educators{\prime} comprehension of students{\prime} emotional states, enabling adaptive teaching strategies and fostering a more personalized learning atmosphere. The findings suggest significant improvements in the student engagement and instructional methods, highlighting the importance of integrating dynamic emotion recognition into online learning platforms for optimized educational outcomes.

articleTitle: Utilising Deep Learning Convolutional Models for the Classification of Brain Tumors in Human Through Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Brain tumor identification at the initial stage is an uphill battle. In a present cut-throat technology era, various medical fields fluke the world by advancing and upgrading technology. Furthermore, by advancing in technics many imaginary things became possible like prediction of brain tumor is possible with MRI reports by using different AI ML algorithms like CNN, R-CNN and many more. Brain tumor occurs because of growth of abnormal tissues in anatomical structure. In this paper authors used MRI image dataset available at github link and apply various deep learning classification algorithms like CNN, PNN and RNN. The results of the experiment conclude that CNN algorithms have highest accuracy 95% with respect to PNN and RNN. All algorithms are tested with 25 hidden layers. This study makes easier for doctors and helps in diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The human nervous system is the controlling mechanism for coordinating all body-related activities. In the cognitive world, it stimulates thinking capabilities. It prompts a reaction to a particular situation and allows body parts to move. In addition, it also regulates other physiological functions such as digestion and respiration. The nervous system consists of billions of cells which interpret information from sensory elements and translate it into coordinated action performed by various parts of the body. With the increase in age, the steady decline of these cells results in a loss of dopamine compounds. Parkinson's disease (PD) is caused by an unforeseen expansion of the movement of bodily extremities that results in this decline. Finding a cure for this disease is still an enormous challenge, and its progression can be slowed by early detection. The proposed work has been implemented with seven machine learning and deep-learning techniques, including decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), logistic regression, naive Bayes, k nearest neighbour, neural network model, and support vector machines for preemptively predicting PD. The model was implemented utilizing a dataset acquired from Kaggle. This included the normal cases as well as those with PD. The findings showed that the random forest model was superior to others, achieving an accuracy of 86.70%. In contrast, the naive Bayes model displayed the lowest accuracy of 71.50%. In addition, both the random forest and support vector machine models showed the highest accuracy levels of 85.90%. Various other performance metrics such as computational time, AUC (the Area Under the Curve), F1-score, ROC curve area, and recall rate were utilized to predict the effectiveness of each technique. Comparative analysis identified that the least performing models are the k-nearest neighbour and naive Bayes methods. In the future, this method can be refined further by using a large dataset and employing deep learning models for higher predictive outcomes.

articleTitle: Motor Imagery Features Selection with Grey Wolf Optimization for Brain Computer Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Feature selection is a significant process in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) that has the potential to significantly enhance system performance, especially if a large number of features are present. Feature selection can help decrease noisy data, overtraining effects, storage needs, and computational complexity thereby enhancing classifier performance. The various feature selection strategies have been reported to attain these objectives. In this work, a hybrid feature selection technique is suggested. It uses a wavelet packet decomposition technique to extract features and grey wolf optimization (GWO) technique to obtain the best subset of features. It is then evaluated with support vector machine (SVM) classifier and obtains maximum classification accuracy of 82.88% for the approximate entropy feature. Experimental findings reveal that the suggested approach outperforms the contemporary MI-BCI systems even with relatively small training data sets.

articleTitle: An Enhanced DarkNet53-based YOLOv3 Feature Pyramid Network for Real-Time Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: With the rapid escalation of automatic and self-driving vehicles, the most efficient, safe, and reliable object detection system has been a big requirement for the automobile industry. These vehicles need an intelligent and highly accurate object detection and recognition system to be implemented for safe and secure driving to avoid road accidents. The ADAS is one of the features in automatic vehicles with improved navigation and object identification performance. Furthermore, better and optimal object detection is also required in surveillance and security along with industrial management and traffic management systems. The proposed work focuses on the development of an object detection model with enhanced and improved capabilities of the deep learning-based YOLOv3 model. This model has been supplied with the learning rate value of 0.001, training batch of 64, decay of 0.0005, and momentum has been set to 0.9. The activation function used in the downsample blocks has been set to either leaky ReLU or linear function. Further, the total number of classes on which the model has been trained is 80 including person, bicycle, car, parking meter, etc. This model is capable of object detection in the images collected from the web. This model has been trained with 80 different classes and testing has been done with the real-time data collected from the websites. This model is capable of dealing with object detection in those images varying from low to high density of the objects. The proposed model can be implemented in traffic light object detection, and ADAS along with security and surveillance applications for enhanced detection and optimal system generation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Enhanced Security in Cyber- Physical Systems: A Multi-Attack Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Today{\prime}s key industries, including energy, healthcare, and transportation, rely heavily on Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) as their foundation. All the same, these systems are seriously threatened by the wide range and growing complexity of cyberattacks. Traditional security measures typically fail when identifying intricate, multi-phase, and unique threats. This research presents a deep learning-based approach to improve CPS{\prime}s resistance against cyber threats. This work aims to detect multiple network attackers with distinct attack natures and provide a novel hybrid architecture. To analyze the performance of the proposed architecture, a publicly available dataset OPC UA is used, which contains Denial of Service (DoS), Man-in-the-middle (MITM), and spoofing attack data. The performance is compared with existing detection frameworks. The findings show a notable increase in detection accuracy over current approaches, underscoring the promise of deep learning strategies in protecting CPS against cyberattacks. This research contributes to cyber-physical security and provides valuable information for implementing intelligent attack detection systems in CPS.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Security of Multimodal Fused Data with Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Blockchain and data fusion synergize for secure, transparent, and optimized integration, revolutionizing information systems and shaping societal dynamics. Proposed solutions involve the implementation of blockchain-based encryption, enforcement of standardized data formats, utilization of decentralized data analysis algorithms, and the development of reward systems on the blockchain. Emphasizing the imperative for further research, the paper underscores the need to assess the feasibility, scalability, and ethical considerations for the successful implementation of these innovative solutions. This research paper delves into the integration of blockchain technology to address key challenges in multimodal data fusion for health monitoring. The study identifies and tackles critical research gaps related to privacy, security, standardization, transparency in data analysis, and incentivizing data sharing. Through this exploration, the research contributes to advancing the security, transparency, and collaborative potential of multimodal health data fusion, thereby fostering more effective and ethical health monitoring practices.

articleTitle: Hybrid Radial Basis Function and Support Vector Machine Model for Precise Breast Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The study is conducted to add a radial basis function (RBF) into the Support Vector Machine (SVM) detection mechanism to increase the accuracy of mammographic image recognition. We resorted to the mammographic images dataset where the data was prepared, augmented, and pre-trained to enhance the model performance. Feature extraction was performed to derive the principal image features and then the feature selection was done to reduce the noisy elements of the dataset to optimize the SVM performance. The SVM model was set up with RBF kernel and also it used Grid search and cross-validation techniques for optimization of gamma and cost parameters to determine the best settings. The integrated RBF-SVM model was better at classifying RBF-SVM compared to models using linear and polynomial kernels. We've got the sensors placed correctly, then the model has 92.22% accuracy, 89.93% precision, 94.52% recall, and 91.5% F1-score. The statistical analysis indeed indicated that the uplift of the model performance parameters was significant with p values minor than 0. 05 or 0. 01. 05. The RBF kernel which was incorporated with the SVM classifier resulted in a better detection of breast cancer in the mammogram class. It is this model with the paramount recall rate (greater than for the other algorithms) that helps clinics diagnose a smaller proportion of malignant cases. The research allows us to conclude that the ML models, particularly the ones with the RBF kernel, are very effective in the process of breast cancer screening as they could highly improve the accuracy and reliability of cancer detection mass screening. The research not only indicates the opportunities for complex AI-based techniques but also points to their usefulness in diagnostic medical applications. Next research should involve verification of the model in different contexts and also seeing to it that the model is implemented into clinical practice and thus ensures it is effective .

articleTitle: Human-Artificial Intelligence Collaboration in HR: Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The alliance between artificial intelligence and human resource professionals is a revolutionary junction that presents both challenging problems and tremendous potential. The applications and challenges of combining human and artificial intelligence in HR are examined in this article. AI is finding its way into HR departments more and more, with uses ranging from improving employee training and hiring procedures to using predictive analytics for workforce planning. The goal of this cooperative synergy is to enhance HR practices' effectiveness, impartiality, and decision-making. However, there are significant challenges to overcome, like Threat to Human Employment, Need for Qualified Applicants, Unethical and Inappropriate Application of Shared Data, Enhancing Employee Turnover between human and AI entities. The paper explores the ever-changing field of HR- related human-AI collaboration, offering insights into emerging applications and challenges that organizations must overcome to realize the full benefits of this revolutionary alliance.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Fake News Detection: An Emperical Investigation of Preprocessing and Modeling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The challenge of identifying fake news through text classification has been met with extensive experimentation to find the best mix of preprocessing techniques and algorithms. Despite efforts, an effective fake news detection model is still out of reach, hindered by model implementation issues and the lack of clean, unbiased data. This situation highlights the need for further research in this area. We investigated many models and approaches for preparing data, including both deep learning algorithms like CNN and LSTM networks and more conventional machine learning algorithms like Random Forest and Gradient Boost. This exploration revealed specific challenges, notably the tendency of automated learning to focus narrowly on individual news items. This paper presents a thorough application of various documented preprocessing techniques and model architectures, aiming to lay a foundation for future research, particularly for newcomers. The performance of these models was tested on two widely used datasets, making a significant contribution to the field of fake news detection. The insights from this study are expected to guide future research and aid in developing more effective detection mechanisms.

articleTitle: Pre-Examination of Breast Cancer Dataset Using Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The breast cancer dataset is thoroughly and insightfully pre-examined using the exploratory data analysis (EDA) method, shedding light on the relationships and traits essential to breast cancer diagnosis. This dataset contains a wide range of features that depict various cell nuclei characteristics extracted from breast mass tissue digital images. The EDA showed that benign and malignant cases were distributed relatively evenly, with the latter having slightly more occurrences. Critical parameters such as mean radius, texture, perimeter, area, smoothness, and compactness exhibited greater values for malignant cases than benign ones. The correlation matrix and heat map highlighted strong relationships between specific traits, indicating their potential value in identifying cancerous or benign cells. Further analysis utilizing scatter plots and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed a definite positive association between the "mean" and "worst" values of each feature, especially for cases of malignancy. Although these results provide a solid basis for constructing prediction models, their usefulness requires model training and evaluation to be confirmed. The EDA offers a compelling starting point for additional, more profound investigation of the data, offering doors for looking at the distributions of the "se" and "worst" features or using different dimensionality reduction methods. The individual objectives and analysis setting are always considered when choosing an exploratory approach.

Author Keywords: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Feature Standardization

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Approaches for Detecting Copy-Move Forgery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The trusted nature of imagery is more easily manipulated in this tech-driven era through copy-move forgery (CMF), when parts of an image are copied and reinserted into the identical frame to trick users. The diversity of visual properties and the complexity of interfering techniques make it difficult to detect such replicas. Currently, there are two major problems facing the present methodologies being used in CMF detection: very expensive processing and poor detection accuracy of complex visual scenarios. In this vein, our article presents a comparative study on the state-of-the-art learning techniques that have been used to address this problem. The current research seeks to outline the limitations of existing CMF detection algorithms which have great tendencies towards false positive signals as well as low precision in recall metrics. Therefore, this study delves deeper into these issues by examining a holistic resolution for their mitigation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Decision Support System for Financial Risk Assessment Using Hybrid Fuzzy Logic and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced framework for financial risk assessment leveraging a synergistic blend of fuzzy logic and machine learning techniques. In today’s volatile financial markets, accurate risk evaluation is imperative for effective decision-making. Traditional methods often fall short in handling uncertainty and complexity inherent in financial data. Hence, this study introduces a novel approach integrating fuzzy logic for handling imprecise information and machine learning algorithms for predictive modeling. The proposed system employs a hybrid model that amalgamates fuzzy inference systems with ensemble learning, harnessing the strengths of both paradigms. Fuzzy logic aids in capturing vague and qualitative aspects of financial risk assessment, while machine learning algorithms like random forests or gradient boosting enhance predictive accuracy by learning from historical patterns and trends. Furthermore, the study presents a comprehensive evaluation using real-world financial datasets to demonstrate the efficacy and superiority of the proposed hybrid approach compared to conventional methods. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall are utilized to validate the system’s effectiveness in risk assessment across different market scenarios. This research contributes to the burgeoning field of financial risk management by providing a robust decision support system capable of handling uncertainties inherent in financial markets, thereby assisting stakeholders in making informed and proactive risk mitigation strategies

articleTitle: Real-time Detection of Students’ Cellphone Usage During Lectures and Behavioral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This research paper explores the application of Computer Vision in the realm of classroom management by addressing the issue of cellphone usage during lectures among students. We present a method for cellphone detection in classrooms during lectures, which can be used to reflect on students’ distraction levels. Using CCTV camera recordings from college classrooms, we created two datasets: one comprising standard lecture recordings and the other capturing an empty classroom environment with only tables visible. Our system utilizes two fine-tuned YOLOv8 models, trained on these datasets, to detect and track students’ cellphone usage patterns. The table detection model maps out all the tables present in the classroom and the cellphone detection model detects cellphones and their users. The cellphone detection model was trained using three variations of YOLOv8: small (s), medium (m), and large (l). The best performing model was YOLOv8m, trained for 55 epochs, achieving an mAP50 of 89.7%. The integration of computer vision technology into classroom management not only supports educators in enforcing cellphone usage policies but also provides valuable insights for optimizing teaching strategies. Our system facilitates behavior analysis by enabling continuous monitoring of students’ cellphone usage over time. Preliminary evaluation of the models shows promising results in accurately detecting and tracking cellphone usage during lectures.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Secured Framework equipped with GI Tagging and Blockchain for Enhanced Data Security and Transparency in Healthcare Operations, for Effective Management of Resources in Government Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Traditional logistics systems lack mainly security and authenticity. In any retail distribution network, ensuring authenticity is the most critical challenge. A customer always look for authenticity and an upcoming / newly introduced retail network lacks the aspect of authenticity. Even though there are various marketing strategies exist to overcome or mellow down the impact of authenticity, the researchers are still not yet came up with any formidable solution. This paper investigates the synergistic mix of blockchain innovation with Geological Sign (GI) labeling, introducing a progressive system for getting and ensuring the legitimacy of locale explicit items. Our answer fosters a protected, straightforward, and sealed framework via flawlessly incorporating different innovations, guaranteeing the evident recognizability of items to their geological beginnings. GI tagging ensures the authenticity of items being included in the transaction network which enhances customer satisfaction and customer belief on the network. By utilizing blockchain's decentralized and changeless record, the joining emphatically works on the viability of GI labeling, giving a comprehensive answer for battling falsifying and unapproved replication. As well as strengthening the security of provincial items, this cooperative structure additionally helps protect social legacy while upgrading shopper trust in the genuineness and nature of these special contributions. The decentralized architecture of blockchain enhances the fault tolerance of the overall system.

articleTitle: NLP-Enabled Bot for Managing Third-Party Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Every organization is becoming increasingly worried about managing the risks associated with third-party services and providers in various sectors. So, in this paper, we introduced an innovative bot that utilizes NLP to aid in third-party risk management. The cutting-edge technology known as natural language processing is set to user in transformative changes to TPRM procedures. This investigation explores the realm of natural language processing bots implemented in the realm of TPRM. By utilizing advanced natural language processing algorithms, the bot sifts through a vast amount of textual data related to contracts, agreements, and conversations with third parties. It then employs machine learning techniques to pinpoint financial risks, security issues, and regulatory violations within these texts. Traditional TPRM methods often prove to be intricate and susceptible to errors. These bots were trained to promptly detect potential vendor threats by scrutinizing vast amounts of unformatted data, including social media conversa- tions and contracts. They simplify document and risk assessments along with other TPRM operations, making the processes more straightforward while bolstering accuracy and paving the way for proactive risk prevention. Here, we will go over the pros and cons of using natural language processing bots in TPRM, with an emphasis on the pros, which include increased efficiency, better risk visibility, and better decision-making skills. In addition, we will go into the latest developments in NLP and how they have affected TPRM. Finally, we will offer practical advice on how to use and control these bots in real-life scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimizing Crop Predictions: A Machine Learning Approach Incorporating Environmental Parameters and Nutrient Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of agriculture, our research pioneers a revolutionary machine-learning approach to redefining crop recommendations, aligning with the tenets of precision agriculture. We delve into a Kaggle dataset, extracting insights from pivotal parameters like Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), pH, temperature, humidity, and rainfall. Navigating two scenarios—Scenario 1, comprehensively considering all parameters, and Scenario 2, zeroing in on indispensable NPK nutrients—we deploy Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. Meticulously trained and evaluated on an 80:20 dataset split, our research conducts a nuanced comparative analysis, unveiling the intricate interplay between environmental variables and nutrient concentrations. With accuracy as the paramount metric, our findings underscore machine learning’s untapped potential in simplifying and elevating crop recommendations, marking a transformative leap forward in precision agriculture. Beyond algorithm intricacies, our study paves the way for sustainable farming, offering indispensable decision support amidst the complexities of modern agriculture. This work encapsulates the transformative role of machine learning in reshaping crop management, steering towards a future characterized by sustainability and efficiency in agriculture.

articleTitle: Smart City: Practice of Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The discussion about smart cities under review about for a long while in established researchers, enterprises, and cultural gatherings, and various audits on the point are available. The term "smart city" alludes to new businesses using data and correspondence advancements alongside the capacities and conditions of metropolitan areas. Discussing about smart city thoughts and analyses towards certifiable acknowledgment, while empowering the mentioned attributes, is a momentum contest. The further empowering of broad smart city facilities and their combination need financially and monetarily solid executions. This will enhance the demands on the designing, sending, activity, upkeep, and development of smart cities.

articleTitle: Secure Communication over IoT Networks using Mutual Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) network transmit the data in an open environment and it can be intercepted by unauthorized users. Different sensors share their data with each other without authentication and it becomes a major security concern. Data privacy and integrity are other security issues. In this paper, a secure communication using mutual authentication model will be introduced to secure the transmisssion over IoT networks. It will isolate the communication between filed sensors and gateways as well as it will also protect the data exchange between gateways and server. Its performance will be analyzed using. Long Range Low powered technology (LoRa) under the constraints of intruder density that varies from 5 to 25 nodes with the legitimate sensors density (100-600)

articleTitle: Advance Facial Analysis: A Hybrid Approach with CNNs, SVMs, and Random Forest for Age and Gender Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: In an era marked by the widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced computer vision technologies, the analysis of facial attributes has become increasingly important across various domains such as access control, video surveillance, and personalized services. A single facial image contains a wealth of demographic information including age, gender, race, and emotional expression. The paper focuses on a unique approach for facial image analysis that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for detailed feature extraction, traditional models like Support Vector Machine for age prediction, and Random Forest also for gender classification. The proposed approach not only addresses existing limitations but also enhances predictive accuracy. The effectiveness of our method was extensively evaluated using the Adience Benchmark dataset, producing outstanding results in both age prediction and gender classification tasks. Through thorough assessments across multiple datasets and evaluation techniques, the proposed solution showcases improved performance as compared to current state of the art methods, affirming its efficacy and reliability.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Empowered Breast Cancer Detection in Images: A YOLO and ResNet-50 Fusion Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: In the world, breast cancer kills more women than any other disease. An accurate forecast model was created, and the highest risk was identified by a data mining-based classification effort that used many approaches. The development of automated breast cancer diagnostic tools has been enabled by advances in data mining and machine learning. It is possible to tell benign breast lesions from malignant ones during a breast cancer diagnosis. More than that, people who have had tumors surgically removed can be given prognoses that tell them when the cancer will return. Consequently, the issues surrounding categorization include these two concerns. There are a lot of data mining techniques used to categorize patients as either "cancerous" or "non-cancerous" in this field. Breast cancer diagnostic concerns are thus encapsulated in the domain of hotly debated classification issues. This work used deep learning to diagnose breast cancer via federated learning while protecting user and hospital data. This study uses YOLO and RestNet-50 DL models. YOLO trains RestNet using client data. The server receives client-trained models for global model integration. Integration gives the client access to the global model for performance evaluation. The suggested model outperforms another state-of-the-art deep learning model in the identical scenario with 98.73% accuracy when all clients receive data equally. The federated research environment has hyper-performance elements like many clients and communication cycles.

articleTitle: eKart: A Cloud-Based E-commerce Platform for Shopping deployed on AWS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The strategic implementation of applications in cloud services has become a crucial strategy for enterprises seeking operational efficiency, scalability, and agility in the quickly changing digital age. The goal of this research is to create and implement a cutting-edge online retail platform on the reliable architecture of Amazon Web Services (AWS). This cloud-based solution, which uses AWS services as its foundation, takes advantage of Amazon EC2 for robust application hosting, guaranteeing unmatched scalability and peak performance. Taking urgent data security considerations into consideration, When AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is used to provide strict access control, Amazon S3 becomes a reliable storage option. In addition to improving operational efficiency, the smooth integration of various AWS services creates a safe and expandable base that is perfect for fostering the development of a vibrant and dynamic e-commerce ecosystem, which is typified by the suggested platform, eKart.

articleTitle: Flood Risk Analysis through Computer Vision and Geometric Correction Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: One of natural calamities is flooding. Research in the creation of flood forecasting models has aided in lowering risk, suggesting an appropriate course of action, minimizing fatalities, and lowering flood-related property damage. The European Space Agency (ESA) sent Sentinel-1 satellite photos that are being used to examine the flood. A variety of filtering and segmentation techniques are used to define the aquifer. This paper provides analysis for explaining flood mapping using image processing methods like calibration; Speckle filtering, binarization and geometric correction using sentinel data 1. After the image processing the output images are analyzed as before and after flood. Sentinel Application Platform can be used for flood mapping.

articleTitle: Effective Machine Learning Model for Disease Recognition and Categorization of Mango Leaves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Maintaining the health and production of mango farms depends on the early detection of illnesses in mango trees. Despite the vital role agriculture plays, it remains an industry receiving limited attention from the machine-learning community. A noteworthy challenge is the lack of standardized and openly accessible agricultural datasets, impeding researchers from fully leveraging the potential of advanced computational prediction tools. The study focuses on employing deep learning and image processing techniques for diagnosing prevalent mango leaf diseases in India. The goal is to enhance both the quality and quantity of agricultural production by implementing effective disease control measures upon identifying plant diseases. The automation of plant disease detection proves particularly beneficial, reducing the monitoring efforts required by large farms. Rapid identification of leaf diseases is crucial, given that leaves serve as a plant's primary source of nutrition. Notably, none of the seven different mango leaf illnesses that have been observed in India have ever been the subject of earlier research. In this study, we provide a lightweight Resnet50 model that can reliably classify healthy mango leaves and the seven discovered illnesses on mango leaves. The performance of our proposed lightweight Resnet-50 model is evaluated against many pre-trained models, such as Exception, Resnet101, and VGG16. The findings reveal that the lightweight Resnet-50 model achieves the highest testing accuracy, reaching an impressive 95%. This underscores the model's effectiveness in automating the identification of mango leaf diseases, offering a promising solution for improving agricultural practices in India.

articleTitle: DocAssist: Signature Perception System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: All In the realm of communication, individuals employ two primary modes: written and spoken language. Handwriting, in particular, serves as a powerful tool for conveying information and emotions across various contexts, including healthcare. Despite its widespread use, deciphering handwritten text remains a challenge due to variations in individual writing styles and the lack of standardization. This challenge is particularly pronounced in the medical field, where handwritten prescriptions can lead to serious consequences if misinterpreted. Our research addresses this issue by proposing DocAssist, a novel model that utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks to achieve an impressive 81% accuracy in recognizing doctors' handwriting. By leveraging machine learning and image recognition technologies, DocAssist aims to enhance prescription legibility, mitigate medication errors, and ultimately improve patient safety and healthcare outcomes. Through rigorous experimentation with the EMNIST dataset, our study demonstrates the effectiveness of DocAssist in accurately interpreting handwritten prescriptions, highlighting its potential to revolutionize prescription processing and alleviate the burden on healthcare professionals and pharmacists.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Role in Internet of Things (IoT) Based Research: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The rapidly growing field of hardware- and software-based connected items that employ communication technologies is known as Internet of Things (IoT). In the past years, IoT utilisation and popularity have increased dramatically across many different applications. IoT stands for new kinds of communication, including communication between two objects and between people and things. Currently, Internet of Things concepts is heavily influencing the online world by introducing a new dimension. Intelligent big data processing and analysis is essential for designing smart IoT applications. Transportation, Logistics, healthcare, agriculture and the environment are examples of such uses. An increase in internet usage and environmental factors outside of the system are causing a dynamic shift in the IoT. Interest in the field of study on employing smart environments to deliver ubiquitous care has grown recently. By tracking the behaviors of their occupants, these smart environments hope to provide comprehensive care through ubiquitous sensing. To make the environment smarter, IoT and machine learning must be used. Machine learning techniques have become more popular in recent years, which encompass tools for extraction, identification, regression, classification, and forecasting. Machine learning is utilised to investigate historical data from cameras and sensors, and techniques are employed to prolong the lifespan of networks. We provide an outline of the recent research in this study being done for various machine learning applications to the Internet of Things. This study's purpose is to survey several IoT technologies that can support smart environment living.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Multiclass Skin Disease Classification: Comparative Assessment of VGG19, YOLOv3, and MobileNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The diagnosis of skin diseases by mere inspection can be a tough ask considering the distinctive and complicated nature of skin lesions. This study looks into the application of three advanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models – VGG19, YOLOv3, and MobileNet – for multiclass skin disease classification, to aid diagnosis accuracy and improve accessibility in the field of dermatology. A comparative study of these models was done with the help of a dataset consisting of images of common skin diseases to assess their diagnostic capabilities. The results demonstrate that VGG19 provides the highest accuracy, which is 0. 928. There is a 95% confidence level and the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) is 0.89 displaying that mobilenet is a powerful tool for feature extraction and class of disease. MobileNet's performance was incredibly strong, but its outperformers were noted for their computational efficiency which makes them suitable for mobile apps. Although YOLOv3, which is mostly intended for object detection, generally functions well with moderately good diagnostic results, this extends the possibility for YOLOv3 application in broad imaging classification tasks. The study showcases the possibility of CNNs in the automated classification of skin disease which can help in reducing the cost by providing more precise and easily-accessible diagnostic solutions. Such tools are not only helpful for the increased accuracy of diagnostics but also for making dermatological services more available, especially for the areas with limited medical expertise.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Mapping of Theme and Trends of IoT and Cloud in the Field of Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric mapping study aimed at understanding the themes and trends of Internet of Things (IoT) and Cloud Computing in the field of education. This paper investigates into the transformative potential of integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and Cloud Computing technologies in the field of education. The exploration focuses on how this integration can revolutionize learning environments by improving accessibility, personalization, and overall efficiency. Emphasizing the opportunities and challenges inherent in this technological convergence. From 2012 to 2023, the analysis reveals several significant trends shaping this evolution from scopus database. The proposed work employs a multifaceted approach, integrating keyword-based word clouds and analyses of documents by year, affiliation, country, type, and subject area. Through systematic data collection from scholarly databases and rigorous bibliometric analysis, the study provides insights into the evolving landscape of IoT and Cloud Computing research in education. Key findings include the identification of prevalent themes, top contributing countries, institutions, and authors, as well as emerging trends and gaps in the literature. The paper concludes the potential implications of IoT and Cloud Computing for educational practice and policy.

articleTitle: Impact of Tuning Parameters for Diagnosing Knee Osteoporosis: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Assessment of osteoporosis is critical for appropriate treatment and management. Prompt identification of osteoporosis, while critical to treating and preventing disease, is frequently ignored because of the necessity for a skilled evaluation. Computerized osteoporosis diagnosis approaches are offered to ease the screening procedure and assist the clinician. Investigators are utilizing deep learning models to diagnose osteoporosis. The majority of these studies emphasize optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNN) to improve their precision. Pre-trained systems are used to circumvent the time-consuming and resource-intensive learning processes required for creating a CNN from beginning. Current research explores eight such models i.e., VGG-19, InceptionV3, Xception, DenseNet169, DenseNet201, Resnet-18, Resnet-101 and Resnet-152. In current research, all underlying CNNs are fine-tuned using the pre-processed collection of data, and both the fine-tuning settings and the pre-trained CNNs are assessed. In terms of accurate classification, ResNet18 outperformed the remaining models by significant margins and exhibited an accuracy of 91.39%, in addition to the greatest precision, recall, and F1-score (95.51%). The fine-tuned version of VGG-19, InceptionV3, Xception, DenseNet169, DenseNet201, Resnet-18, Resnet-101 and Resnet-152 outperformed the legacy version by 2.69%, 4.84%, 4.84%, 2.15%, 1.61%, 2.14%, 3.22% and 2.14%, respectively exhibiting a clear edge in classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Based Engine Oil Condition Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: This paper presents the development of ultrasonic based engine oil condition monitoring system. The developed system will qualitatively detect the deterioration in the engine oil quality due to the dissolved impurities developed over its usage in the engine. The test set up consists of an ultrasonic sensor interfaced with the Arduino Uno microcontroller board that is placed at a fixed height over the beaker in which different samples of engine oil at constant volume are taken. The deterioration of engine oil is quantitatively analyzed by measuring the distance travelled by the ultrasonic waves in different samples of engine oil. The samples of engine oil is collected over its usage with the distance covered by the automobile. Using test bed the distance travelled by the ultrasonic wave is monitored for different samples of engine oil. It is experimentally verified from the test set-up that the concentration of dissolved impurities in the oil is inversely proportional to the distance covered by ultrasonic waves. As the distance measured below the threshold value, which is proportional to high concentration of impurities in engine oil, it is concluded that the condition of oil is poor and needs to be replaced by the pristine engine oil. Therefore, the developed system will aid in increasing the useful life of automobile engine. Furthermore, the same set-up can also be used to benchmark the quality of engine oil provided by different manufacturers.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a potent instrument that utilizes human knowledge to solve difficult problems more quickly. Through the application of AI algorithms that examine vast amounts of biological data, such as proteomics and genomics, scientists are able to pinpoint targets linked to disease and anticipate how those targets may interact with possible therapeutic candidates. This makes it possible to approach drug discovery in a more effective and focused manner, which raises the possibility of successful drug approvals. Additionally, by streamlining research and development procedures, AI can help lower development costs. This capacity lessens the need for extensive and expensive animal research by enabling the prioritization and optimization of lead compounds. Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that evaluate real-world patient data can support personalized medicine strategies, improving patient adherence and treatment outcomes. This analysis highlights the advantages and disadvantages of the several AI-based techniques used in pharmaceutical technology. However, the pharmaceutical industry's ongoing exploration and investment in AI present great opportunities for improving patient care and drug development procedures.

articleTitle: Securing Sustainable Energy Trading: An RSA-Encrypted IoT Solution for Smart Meter Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Smart grids have been replacing conventional energy grids in recent years and are deemed the next generation of today’s power infrastructure distribution. However, due to the digitization of the energy grid framework, smart grids are prone to multiple cyber threats such as phishing attacks and data breaches. The number of cyberattacks against smart meters is estimated to have risen from 6,000 to 7,900 by 2023 and is expected to rise further in the coming years. These attacks allow attackers to manipulate access to the smart meter, thus leaking sensitive information. This paper proposes a Rivest–Shamir–Adleman (RSA) encryption algorithm to securely encrypt the data of the telemetry received, which is then sent to the servers. The received data is displayed to the user via an application. The need to maintain the integrity of the financial transactions in energy trading points to the importance of cyber security. This plays a major role in the construction of a sustainable community which is empowered with energy trading. Implementation of a secure algorithm like RSA enhances the security and resilience of the transactions.

articleTitle: DevConnect: Knowledge Sharing Social Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: "DevConnect" aims to create an interactive platform tailored for developers to collaborate, seek assistance, and discover new projects seamlessly. Through its innovative features, developers can engage in meaningful collaborations, exchange messages for help queries, and explore fresh project ideas effortlessly. At the heart of the platform lies its ability to facilitate collaboration among developers, a vibrant community where knowledge sharing thrives. Users can reach out to fellow developers for assistance, feedback, or guidance, enriching their development journey with valuable insights and support. Central to the platform{\prime}s functionality is its robust search feature, enabling developers to explore a diverse range of projects based on their interests, skills, and preferences. Whether seeking inspiration for a new endeavour or searching for specific project types, developers can easily navigate the platform to discover exciting opportunities. Furthermore, developers have the option to follow their favourite peers, allowing them to stay updated on their latest projects, contributions, and insights. This feature not only cultivates a sense of camaraderie within the community but also empowers developers to build meaningful connections and expand their networks. The Social Media Showcase project is designed with user-friendliness in mind, ensuring that developers can effortlessly navigate the platform and access its wealth of resources. With its intuitive interface and seamless functionality, developers can focus their energy on what matters most: innovation and collaboration. By providing a dynamic and interactive space for developers to connect, share, and discover, the Social Media Showcase project seeks to enrich the development community and inspire creativity in the ever-evolving landscape of technology.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Sleep Apnea Detection And Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Sleep apnea, a common yet underdiagnosed sleep disorder, causes a person’s breathing repeatedly stops and starts, which poses serious health risks if left untreated. Existing diagnostic methods are often inconvenient, expensive, and inaccessible to many individuals. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an AI-powered system DreamGuardian for the early detection and prediction of sleep apnea. This system utilizes a combination of machine learning algorithms and advanced signal processing techniques to analyze data from non-invasive sensors integrated into a wearable device. These sensors monitor various physiological signals during sleep, including respiratory patterns, heart rate variability, and movement, enabling comprehensive sleep analysis in real-time. The methodology that we have followed for sleep apnea detection and prediction involves acquiring a diverse dataset from sleep clinics and repositories, formatting it, and selecting key features based on existing literature. Non-invasive sensors are integrated into a wearable device prototype to monitor physiological parameters. Standardized protocols are developed for data collection, and ethical considerations are being followed. The data collected from the users will be analysed using a machine learning algorithm. The system accurately predicts the presence or absence of sleep apnea based on variables such as heart rate, BMI, age, gender, respiratory rate, ESS score, AHI, and oxygen saturation.

articleTitle: Impact of Climate Change on Rainfall Pattern by using Ridge Regression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The research aims to ridge regression modelling to investigate the rainfall trends and temporal patterns of the variability the very comprehensive understanding of the precipitation dynamics. Ridge regression which is an improved technique, is utilized to improve the predictive accuracy by reducing multi-collinearity (MC) and overfitting problems. The study analyzes the temporal variations of the rainfall and attempts at finding the patterns and trends of the evolution. The rainfall changes as well as the influence of the climate change parameters are taken into consideration. Through balancing bias and variance, ridge regression has proven instrumental in improving robustness of predictions, thereby making a big difference in valid rainfall forecasting. The paper enriches the knowledge base in hydrology as well as climate science as it presents detailed findings on the rainfall event over a period of time, which are crucial for proper water resource management and climate study. These discoveries show the way towards more accurate models for rainfall forecasts, which could support better decision making on a rainfall related matter. In addition to that, this study also provides evidence that ridge regression is an efficient method for capturing highly complex temporal processes, which underlines its usefulness for expanding the level of understanding of climate-related issues. Overall, the studies agree on the role of data collection methods in rainfall analysis adding to the understanding of precipitation temporal variation which contributes to water resource planners and climate resilience promotion.

articleTitle: Improving the Longevity of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) via FCMA: Fuzzy-C Means Clustering with A-Star Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Mostly all the sensors are battery-operated, so energy utilization becomes a crucial and critical issue in WSNs. As battery power is constrained in real life scenarios; thus to make the efficient selection of sensor nodes from the particular application environment form Source to Target is of utmost concern. Deploying sensor nodes close to the sink is challenging, leading to multi-hop transmission due to the proportional energy usage as a function of distance from the sink node. To resolve this issue, this work proposes a combined approach using Fuzzy-C Means clustering with the A-star algorithm. This hybrid method takes care for efficient energy utilization and enhances the network lifespan. The implementation plan consists of two sections: The first section involves clustering in WSNs using the Fuzzy-C Means method. The second section utilizes the A-star algorithm with fuzzy-inference. Metrics like minimum hops and residual energy, represented as Distant level and Energy level respectively, are considered in this proposed plan.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring System for Campus Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Air quality significantly impacts people's health, especially in indoor spaces like homes, schools, colleges, offices, etc. Even though air quality is essential, most educational campuses do not have a thorough monitoring system. As a result, staff and students may be exposed to health risks and unaware of the air quality they breathe. An Air Quality Monitoring System is desperately needed to improve indoor air quality. This paper aims to improve people's productivity and wellbeing in indoor environments by filling the current void in educational institutions' air quality monitoring. The suggested system helps to increase awareness of the significance of indoor air quality among staff, instructors, and students, in addition to acting as a real-time monitoring tool. Informed decision-making for preserving a safe and comfortable learning environment is made possible by analyzing the gathered data to find trends and patterns. The experiments were carried out at the PIET Campus in Panipat. The system was checked at the home location for usage and accuracy. By putting this comprehensive air quality monitoring system into indoor spaces, especially educational institutions, we can proactively address any health risks related to poor air quality and make the learning environment safer and more comfortable for everyone.

articleTitle: LSTM Networks for Improved Stock Price Prediction: A Comparison of Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon Stocks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Stock price prediction remains a critical endeavor in financial markets, facilitating informed decision-making for investors and analysts. In this research, we present an innovative approach utilizing (LSTM) networks to forecast future stock prices for three prominent companies: Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft. Our model leverages historical stock price data spanning from January 2013 to January 2022, focusing on the closing prices of the respective stocks. By employing LSTM networks with stacked layers and dropout regularization, our methodology aims to capture intricate temporal dependencies inherent in stock price movements. The performance of our model is very much measured with the most crucial metrics such as(MSE), (RMSE) and (MAE). Through a comparison of our performed analyses we show the effectiveness of our approach in the generate of the accurate forecasts for the next trading day. Notably, our results indicate superior predictive performance for Amazon stock, followed by Apple and Microsoft. This research contributes to the advancement of predictive modeling techniques in financial forecasting and offers valuable insights for investors and financial analysts seeking to optimize their investment strategies. Further exploration of LSTM-based approaches holds promising potential for enhancing stock price prediction accuracy and informing decision-making in the dynamic landscape of financial markets.

articleTitle: Exploring Innovations in Speech Recognition: An in-depth Analysis and Real-world Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Speech recognition, a field with a rich history, enables computers to accurately transcribe spoken words captured via a microphone, facilitating human-computer interaction. In the last ten years, speech recognition has become much better by using deep neural networks. These networks replaced old methods and improved how accurately computers understand speech. We have used DeepSpeech2 model for speech recognition and added some changes which helps computers understand different kinds of speech, like accents and noisy backgrounds. Deep learning has played a big role in making this happen. It helps computers learn from sound directly and makes them better at understanding speech. Overall, these improvements mean that computers can now understand speech much better, no matter how it sounds. Recurrent Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks had also played crucial roles in this advancement, learning patterns from sequential data, and enhancing system robustness. These innovations have led to more accurate and adaptable speech-to-text systems, fostering broader applications, and meeting diverse user needs and convert into more simpler words which helped us to achieve error rate of 17 percent.

articleTitle: Multimodal Data Extraction & Fusion for Health Monitoring System and Early Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: Multimodal data fusion involves combining varied data types to enhance analysis, yielding comprehensive insights and improving decision-making in diverse applications. Current literature tends to focus on individual aspects, lacking a holistic perspective. A lack of standardized frameworks for effective multimodal fusion hampers seamless integration. Bridging these gaps is imperative to unlock the full potential of multimodal data fusion, ensuring more accurate diagnostics, personalized interventions, and improved patient outcomes. This research paper delves into Multimodal Data Fusion for Health Monitoring, acknowledging the significant strides made in the field while highlighting pertinent research gaps. The study emphasizes the need for a comprehensive understanding of the dynamic interactions between various data modalities and their impact on healthcare outcomes. This paper identifies these critical research gaps and serves as a guide for future investigations, steering the field toward a more robust and integrated approach to health monitoring.

articleTitle: AI for Tourism: Pioneering New Frontiers in the Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
abstract: The conversational agents or chatbots have become a part of our everyday life and are designed to make our life easier. Recent advancements in natural language processing and artificial intelligence have made them surge past the popularity of social media apps as they can understand and process more information and respond more intelligently. Chatbots have covered most of the consumer and business markets and help these sectors gain huge profits due to customer engagements. In this paper we intend to provide such engaging and interactive services in the tourism industry as well. This is intended to boost the number of tourists every year thus giving a boost to the tourism sector which will further help and improve economic growth too.
